text.p: Harvesting of the Kansas wheat crop was completed during the week ended Sunday, the state's agricultural statistics service said Monday in its weekly crop progress report.
Harvesting was 100 percent complete, ahead of 97 percent last year and 93 percent on average.
Corn was 60 percent silked, against 81 percent last year and the average of 59 percent. Corn condition was rated 85 percent good to excellent, down from 88 percent last week.
Sorghum condition was reported as 80 percent good to excellent, against 86 percent at that level last week.
Sixteen percent of the sorghum was headed, ahead of 12 percent last year and the average of seven percent.

Soybean blooming was 52 percent complete, ahead of 49 percent last year and the average of 33 percent. Eighty-four percent of soybeans were in good to excellent condition, against 85 percent at that level a week ago.
The state's sunflower crop was rated 76 percent good to excellent. Figures for the previous week were unavailable.
Topsoil moisture condition was rated nine percent surplus, 48 percent adequate, 32 percent short and 11 percent very short.
